spec.agency.evidence: [沙王·codex] 规格6–7.5秒：我将敌人仅逼退半步，就“不再理它们”并连续起伏蓄力，树人仍扑上来抽打我；我想完成砸地施法，但这一拍没有写我挨打后的反应、防护或承受攻击仍能施法的条件，也没有被控制的说明。无法确认我的行为符合受击应对要求。；[树人·claude] Every beat makes sense from my side as a treant. From 0 to 1.5 s the four of us charge it at full speed from about 15 m out and arrive with branch arms raised, so we act from the first moment instead of waiting. From 1.5 to 6 s we take turns lashing its shell about every 0.8 s and no one stands still. When a blade hits me the bark flips open and wood chips fly, and its carapace shoves me back, so getting hit has a visible reaction. From 6 to 7.5 s it sweeps us back half a step and starts winding up, and we use the opening to rush in and lash it again; that is a reasonable attack, not freezing in place. From 7.8 s the heaving ground throws us around and flying clods hit us, which makes this a passive, effectively controlled stretch. Our deaths from 8.5 to 10 s are forced by the waves, not us lining up to die. In image 1 the treants at upper left and on the right are being thrown sideways by the heaving ground, and the one at lower left has already fallen, which matches being swept away. One weak point: from 7.8 s until we die, the script never says whether we try to brace or get away. It only gives the passive state 'thrown around', but that is close to a control state, so I still pass this.

spec.agency.evidence: [沙王·codex] 图1中我低伏、铲刃微张、尾针高翘，已处于戒备姿势。规格0–1.5秒敌人尚在接近，我保持迎敌姿态；1.5–6秒进入近身交战后，我横扫、尾刺、顶开敌人，持续反击；6–7.5秒我先逼退敌人再蓄力，挨打时护住头甲、甲壳震动、身体晃动，有防御和受击反应；7.5–7.8秒砸地释放技能。7.8–10.8秒敌人已被震荡波掀翻控制，我伏地观察、让连续波发挥作用，暂不追击说得通；10.8–13秒起身巡视确认战果，13–15秒稳定收势。；[树人·claude] Speaking as one of the treants, the script holds up. 0–1.5s: four of us charge from about 15 m away and raise our branch arms once we're 3–4 m from it. 1.5–6s: we take turns whipping its shell, and getting bark peeled open by its blades counts as a reaction. 6–7.5s: we see it charging up and pile in to hit it while it's open, which makes sense. From 7.8s we're thrown around by the heaving ground, which the script explicitly lists as being controlled. 8.5–10s we die. Nowhere does it ask us to stand idle or line up to die. The problem is that image 1 (the first frame) doesn't show us charging. The treant on the left (about x230, y390) and the one at top left (about x490, y150) are both upright with their root feet close together and their arms hanging loose like claws. They look like they're standing still or just strolling, not running flat out. Only the two on the right (about x1250, y240 and x1470, y500) have their roots slightly apart, and that reads as walking, not sprinting. Starting from this frame, the model will probably make us stand around or wander for 0–1.5s, which contradicts the script's 'charging at full speed on our roots'. A smaller issue in image 2 (peak frame): the bottom-right treant (about x1100–1550, y650–850) is lying face down with its arms stretched forward. That looks like the banned 'treant falls forward', not 'collapses backward to the side and lies on its side'. It may lead the model to make us fall the wrong way. I'm marking this fail.

The bottom-left treant is about 430 px because it's close to the camera, and with the high angle compressing height I can't fully separate depth. I'm not certain, so it's a fail. On the text: 'as tall as a grown man' for the treants roughly agrees with 1.9 m, but the image's ratio doesn't match the card.

spec.status_visual.evidence: [fidelity·claude] The spec gives the slow a visible marker: a wide, translucent, bright yellow-lime pulse band about 2–3 m across, with radial streaks, that briefly lights the ground and the treants yellow-green as it passes. That matches image 1, MW 11:27.75–11:28.50 and SG 0:08.20–0:09.00, where the original is a thick, soft, translucent yellow glow band with radial streaks. The marker is also not in the negative prompt. However, in image 5 (the peak frame) the yellow-lime is several thin, sharp, bright lines tracing the edges of cracks. They read as glowing crack lines, not the wide translucent pulse band with radial streaks from the original. The four treants are also not lit yellow-green: they stay dark brown, and the treant on the right and the one in the upper left have almost no yellow on them. So the peak frame does not draw the marker to the original's look. I also can't confirm the spec's claim that 'units in the original have no separate slow marker' (it cites ref/refs.md). The thumbnails in image 1 are too low-resolution to show whether units carry a debuff marker, and in TS 32:22.17–32:22.50 there is a bright cyan-blue blob near the hero whose source I can't tell. Because I'm not sure on this point, I'm marking it fail.
